supplementary_review_outcomes: Safran Electrical & Power: a 2020 Safran announcement shows it manufactured the wiring harness for the XSun SX 1.2 pre-series drone. Historical UAV-specific work at the named subsidiary, so the categorical exclusion was softened to needs_review.

Sopra Steria / CS Group: CS Group's BOREADES is its own C-UAS system, deployed since 2015 with more than 50 operational systems. CS Group is already verified separately; the Sopra Steria parent-level hold stands, with the evidence recorded.
SLM Solutions: the squeeze-out was registered 1 September 2023, not 4 September, which was the announcement. Description corrected.
Ricardo: the exclusion and the Ricardo Mendes correction stand. A 2010 Wolverine UAV engine line existed at the US subsidiary Ricardo Inc; historical and not attached to the UK record.

phase.name: merits verification
phase.goal_met: Every backlog candidate has an evidence-based disposition: verified, excluded, or held with a written reason. The only records without one are the four waiting on the warhead decision.
not_selected: discovery of the six absent companies

disagreements: Bulba: IN_SCOPE declined. The research itself calls it a manufacturer brand rather than an independent legal company, and the named manufacturer Servis Budtrans has no record here. Admitting it would repeat the Bullspike error from Batch 12.
Fulltime Robotics: IN_SCOPE declined. Maturity is prototype and demonstration, the same rule that held Frenel Imaging, Dryad and Asseco. Its only link was a LinkedIn post, not recorded as a website.
batch_16.data_cleanup: Twelve Ukrainian directory imports were tagged with the bare root UAV category and no evidence. Four proved real and were given capability leaves and named products; eight could not be confirmed. All unevidenced root UAV tags were deleted from remaining candidates.
ownership_checks: Grupo Oesia excluded as a parent: the autopilots belong to UAV Navigation SLU, already verified with the alias UAV Navigation-Grupo Oesia.
FLANQ held: ORKA, ORKA Dock and ORKA Dock Mini are already recorded under CiS.
TNO excluded on entity type: Destinus and Robin Radar, its industrialisation partners, are already verified and own the products.
Twist Robotics OBRIY given a distinct slug; an unrelated Obriy 2.0 belongs to Kara Dag.
batch_16.sensor_rule_outcome: smartmicro, PCO, Senop and AIM admitted on named drone-specific variants; Acconeer, Blickfeld and ams OSRAM excluded as general-purpose parts used in demonstrations. The Batch 13 rule separated them cleanly.

verification_pool.note: Empty. Do not manufacture a batch 19. The four remaining candidates need a human scope decision, not research.

batch_17.agreement_with_research: 39 of 40 - the closest of the run
disagreements: Liebherr Aerospace: UNKNOWN upgraded to verified. The hold was about entity mapping and the record is already filed as Germany, matching Liebherr-Aerospace Lindenberg GmbH. A contracted Eurodrone landing-gear programme is the same basis on which Avio Aero was admitted in Batch 15 for the Catalyst engine on the same aircraft.
batch_17.new_record_defect_found: Composite labels. TUBITAK UZAY / ASELSAN and OHB Italia / Leonardo are programme and consortium labels joining two organisations with a slash, not companies. Both constituents already exist separately and ASELSAN is verified with fifty products. A question about composite labels was added to Batch 18.
ownership_discipline: Quantum Frontline Industries attached to Frontline Robotics existing Linza product as a manufacturer rather than given a duplicate; the design credit stays with Frontline.
Hevi Optronics admitted for its own platform; the KENIS sensor stays with HENSOLDT.
Oxford Space Systems excluded partly because its drone testing uses Quadsat equipment, and Quadsat is verified separately.
batch_17.exclusion_shape: Nine of nineteen exclusions were space companies. The scoring model has no notion of altitude: a synthetic-aperture radar reads the same at 400 metres and 400 kilometres.

disagreements: Grupo Amper: UNKNOWN upgraded to verified. The hold was over which group entity owns the C-UAS C2 system; this catalogue holds exactly one Spanish Amper record and the product page is on its own domain, so there is no subsidiary here to duplicate.

Diehl Aviation: UNKNOWN downgraded to excluded. The hold was over which Diehl entity owns the cited ARES work; Diehl Aerospace and Diehl Defence are separate verified records here. What is left for the Aviation division is a demonstrator.
batch_18.csv_defect: The researched CSV arrived with a tool-output truncation banner written into the top of the file (three junk lines before the header) and row 18 (KNDS Robotics) truncated mid-cell so its columns shifted. The banner was stripped. The KNDS disposition was recovered from the batch-18 research report, not guessed, and the reconciliation CSV records the row as damaged.
product_ownership_corrections: MISTRAL 3 moved from CS Group to MBDA France. CS Group is a C2 integrator and does not build missiles.
BOREADES created for CS Group, the counter-UAV system it has actually sold since 2015, which was missing. CS Group keeps its verified status either way.
Fulgur moved from Leonardo to MBDA Italia, which the Italian Defence Ministry names as the contracted developer.
Threat-Sense attached to Pearson Engineering. The product row had no company at all.
Tactical Core Middleware moved from Rheinmetall to blackned, whose own record already named it.
batch_18.not_created: GULL ONE E. A product called GULL already belongs to ARMMO Defense Technologies here and the original designer is unconfirmed, so INFINTEQ was admitted on its ground control stations alone.
batch_18.third_composite_label: Thales Alenia Space Italia / e-GEOS, matching the two found in Batch 17.
